# Pages and publishing

The pages you read during the week, how they are rendered from your data,
the checks that keep them fresh, and how `pages publish` gets them to
your phone. Read this when a page looks stale, when the coach's write
line names a commit, or when you want to know what the dashboard counts.

## Rendered pages: edit the data, then re-render

Every page is rendered from structured data, never written by hand. A
rendered file starts with a marker that names its source and the command
that rewrites it:

```text
<!-- generated by coach from data/state.json as of 2026-10-12T09:00:00Z; edit the data, then run: python3 -m coach pages render -->
```

The rule is in the marker: edit the data, then run the command. A page
that reads history carries an as-of time, so a fresh render at that time
reproduces it exactly and a page goes stale only when its inputs change,
not when a day passes. A hand edit to a page is caught by the freshness
checks below and overwritten at the next render.

## The dashboard (`README.md`)

The dashboard is where you stand this week, and the page GitHub shows
first on a phone. In your workspace `README.md` is this page; the
template's README is its front page, and the first `pages render`
replaces it only when the coach asks you and runs `--replace-readme`.

The page has, in order:

- a status block of at most six lines: the brief's header line (the
  week, the rotation position when the program rotates, the phase when
  nutrition is on, and the next check-in's date and tier); the block
  line (block number, completed hard weeks of the ceiling, fatigue
  triggers, light-week state); the last check-in with a link; the
  consistency line; the as-of time as "Updated";
- the week's sessions, every lifting session, coach-led session and
  activity by date with a Done column;
- `## Watch`, the same items as the brief's Watch;
- `## Progress`, at most five lines: up to three best e1RMs, the
  core-complete streak, and the latest bodyweight;
- `## Links` to the brief, the progress page, the latest check-in, the
  program, all check-ins, and the template's README for how this works.

This is the `pages` fixture instance's dashboard as of 12 October 2026,
from `pages show dashboard`:

```markdown
<!-- generated by coach from data/state.json as of 2026-10-12T09:00:00Z; edit the data, then run: python3 -m coach pages render -->
# Training dashboard

- **Week of 12 Oct** · Check-in due Sun 18 Oct (deep)
- Block 1 · 2 of 6 hard weeks · triggers 0 of 4 · light week: not due
- Last check-in: [Sun 11 Oct (weekly)](check-ins/2026-10-11.md)
- Consistency: 4 of 4 planned sessions trained in 2 completed ordinary weeks (28 Sep – 11 Oct); a full count takes 4
- Updated Mon 12 Oct 09:00 (UTC)

| Day | Session | Tier | Key | Done |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mon 12 | Session A | core | Back Squat 3×5 @ 100 kg |  |
| Thu 15 | Session B | core | Single Arm Row 3×10 @ 30 |  |

## Watch

- Nothing flagged.

## Progress

- Best e1RM (estimated one-rep max): Back Squat 122 kg (5 Oct 2026)
- Best e1RM: Bench Press 32 kg/hand (5 Oct 2026)
- Best e1RM: Single Arm Row 42 kg (1 Oct 2026)
- Core-complete streak (weeks with every core session trained): none counted yet

## Links

- [This week's brief](this-week.md)
- [Progress](progress.md)
- [Latest check-in](check-ins/2026-10-11.md)
- [Program](routine/program.md)
- [All check-ins](check-ins/)
- [How this works](https://github.com/joeuk89/claude-strength-coach#readme)
```

**Consistency** (see [the glossary](../../CONTEXT.md)) leads the
dashboard: planned sessions trained of those planned over the last four
completed ordinary weeks, with the weeks it left out and why ("left out:
week of 21 Sep (illness)"). It covers completed weeks only, so this
week's sessions stay in the table. Coach-led sessions count; optional
sessions, sessions on a planned break and sessions the trainer cancelled
do not. Fewer than four ordinary weeks show as a shorter count ("a full
count takes 4"), never as misses, and no percentage is shown.

**A core-complete week** is a stricter count: every planned core session
of the week's overlay was trained, logged or not, and no coach-led
session is recorded as not having happened. Optional sessions never
count. A coach-led session nobody recorded, or one the trainer
cancelled, neither counts nor breaks it. Consecutive core-complete weeks
make the streak the dashboard and the progress page show, with the
longest streak beside it. A week with no planned core session ends a
streak without counting as missed.

**The Watch section** draws on three sources, at most three items by
priority: unresolved flags on the week's overlays that block or warn;
each niggle aggravated, watching or easing on the brief's date, with an
escalating one told to have it assessed by a qualified professional; and
the block's state, a fatigue watch, a proposed, declined or skipped light
week. An item that repeats another shows once. When nothing is open it
says "Nothing flagged."

## This week's brief (`this-week.md`)

The brief is the one-page statement of the current week, rewritten every
programming pass. It is at most 60 lines, and its sections come in this
order:

- the header line: the week, the rotation position and whether it is
  confirmed, the phase, and the next check-in's date and tier;
- `## Focus`: the overlay's week focus, then one line per planned break
  overlapping the week and the day training resumes. With nutrition on,
  a food line follows: the protein floor, last week's average, the
  anchors and any override;
- `## Sessions`: the whole week by date, lifting sessions first on each
  day, then coach-led sessions, then activities. Key names the first
  exercise and its working sets; Done shows ✔, ✗, "✔ moved to Tue 13"
  or blank for a day still to come. The session sheets link follows the
  table when Hevy is off;
- `## Changed`: up to five lines of what changed and why, priority
  lifts first, each in your words ("light week", "agreed with your
  coach", "eased back after 14 days off", or the progression's own
  reason), then "and N more in the check-in";
- `## Watch`: the same items as the dashboard;
- `## If you miss a day`: one line per missed-day rule in the program,
  or one line saying there are none yet;
- `## Wins`: up to three: a new best e1RM in the last seven days, a
  core-complete streak of two weeks or more, or every core session
  trained last week.

Over 60 lines, items are cut from the end of Wins, then Watch, then
Changed, then If you miss a day. Sessions and Focus are never cut. A
dumbbell change that ends on a per-hand load gets the Hevy value
appended: `22.5 → 25/hand (Hevy: 50)`. See [Hevy](hevy.md) for the two
numbers.

## The progress page (`progress.md`)

The progress page starts with a table of every lift with an e1RM series:
best e1RM and its date, the latest, and the change over 28 days. When a
program slot keeps a training max, `## Training maxes` names it. Then
`## Consistency` repeats the dashboard's count as a sentence and lists
every week counted or left out, oldest first, with sessions trained of
planned. `## Core-complete weeks` gives the current and longest streak
and the last 12 weeks as ✔ and ✗. `## Bodyweight` shows weekly means of
the last 12 weeks, naming the basis (trend weight or scale weight) and
the sources.

## The session sheets (`this-week-sheets.md`)

With Hevy off, `sheets render` writes one section per session of the
week's overlay: title and date, the session focus, a table of sets ×
reps, load, RPE, rest and an empty Done column, then each exercise's
guidance. Loads show your number only (`25/hand`). A null load prints
"choose the load". The footer explains how to report the workout in
chat, and a beginner's sheets end with a short RPE and rep-range key. A
sheet rendered from an unapproved overlay says "Not approved yet". See
[Training without Hevy](training-without-hevy.md).

## The routine pages (`routine/`)

`program render` writes `routine/program.md` and one page per session
from `data/program.json`. They describe the program as written; the
week's actual loads are in the brief and the overlay. Never edit them:
edit the program data, validate, then render.

## Rendered regions inside check-in records

A check-in record is prose you and the coach write around regions the
scripts render. A region sits between two markers that name its kind
and id:

```text
<!-- coach:begin week-review 2026-10-04 -->
...
<!-- coach:end week-review 2026-10-04 -->
```

| Region | Kind | Written by | What it holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| Week in review | `week-review <record date>` | `checkin skeleton`, refreshed with `--refresh` | The window, sessions trained of planned, misses, coach-led sessions, and the e1RM table. Only the newest record's region is kept fresh; older ones are archive. |
| The week ahead | `overlay <overlay id>` | `overlay render <id> --into <record>` | The approved week's tables: sets, loads, RPE, rest, changes and notes per session. |
| Cardio block | `cardio <week label>` | `cardio render --week W --into <record>` | The week's runs, conditioning and session-RPE load. A snapshot with no freshness check. |

The deep check-in's follow-up section is different: `followups render
--deep --date D` prints it and the coach pastes the text into the
record, with no markers. Recipe cards and research notes hold regions of
kind `card` and `research` in the same way.

## Meal plan pages and the recipe index

`meals render <id>` writes `nutrition/plans/<id>.md` from the plan's
data; `recipes render` rewrites each card's rendered region and
`nutrition/menu/index.md` from the cards' data blocks. See [Recipes and
meal plans](recipes-and-meal-plans.md).

## The render commands

| Command | Writes |
|---|---|
| `pages render [--only brief\|dashboard\|progress] [--replace-readme]` | `this-week.md`, `README.md` and `progress.md` as of now. Refuses (exit 3) to overwrite a `README.md` the coach did not generate unless `--replace-readme` is given. Reports `brief_overlay`: the overlay the brief shows and whether it is approved. |
| `pages show brief\|dashboard\|progress` | Nothing: prints the page as a fresh render would write it. |
| `sheets render [--overlay ID]` | `this-week-sheets.md` from the brief's overlay, else the next to start. |
| `program render` | `routine/program.md` and one page per session. |
| `overlay render ID [--into FILE]` | The week-ahead region; with `--into`, into that record. |
| `checkin skeleton --date D [--refresh]` | A new record with its week-review region, or with `--refresh` only the regions of an existing one. |
| `cardio render --week W [--into FILE]` | The cardio block; with `--into`, into that record. |
| `meals render ID` | `nutrition/plans/<id>.md`. |
| `recipes render [slug]` | Each card's region and the index. |
| `research render [ID]` | One note's region, or every note's. |

## The freshness checks

`coach check` fails when a rendered file or region differs from a fresh
render:

| Check | Guards |
|---|---|
| `pages_fresh` | The three root pages, each at its own as-of time. A `README.md` the coach did not generate is not checked. |
| `pages_line_ceiling` | `this-week.md` over 60 lines. |
| `sheets_render_fresh` | The session sheets; skipped with Hevy on. |
| `routine_render_fresh` | The routine pages. |
| `overlay_render_fresh` | The week-ahead regions in records whose span has not ended. |
| `recipe_render_fresh`, `recipe_index_fresh` | Card regions and the index. |
| `meal_plan_render_fresh` | Meal plan pages. |
| `research_render_fresh` | Research note regions. |
| `render_fresh_sweep` | Any other marked region in the workspace. |

The PostToolUse hook runs the right ones the moment a page or record is
edited by hand, so the coach hears about a stale region at once and
re-renders it instead of leaving it. See
[Configuration](configuration.md) for the hook.

## The commit plan and `pages publish`

Publishing is the only push the coach makes without being asked, and
one "go" approves it. At the end of a programming pass the coach's brief
ends with a write line naming each Hevy routine, any program edit, and
"Commit: <paths>" or "Commit: no training records". Those paths are the
commit plan (see [the glossary](../../CONTEXT.md)): the training records
that will be committed with the week, file by file, both those already
changed and those the approved write steps will write.

`pages plan` computes it, read-only. The records eligible are
`data/state.json`, `data/decisions.json`, `data/blocks.json` and files
under `data/log/`, `data/history/` and `routine/`, plus
`data/program.json` only when the brief names a structural change. The
coach passes a flag for each step "go" will run, so the plan names what
those steps write before they have:

| Flag | Step "go" runs | Paths named |
|---|---|---|
| `--structural [--session ID]...` | the program edit and `program render` | `data/program.json`, `routine/program.md`, each session's page |
| `--light-week` | `block decide --outcome adopted` | `data/blocks.json`, `data/decisions.json`, `data/state.json`, `routine/program.md` |
| `--one-off` | setting or clearing the one-off week | `data/state.json` |
| `--create-routines` | `routines create` | `data/state.json` |
| `--missed` | `missed apply` | `data/history/annotations.json` |

`config.toml`, `profile.md`, `.env` and other files never join the plan.

After the writes, the coach runs `pages render` and then `pages publish
--overlay <id>` with `--include <path>` for each path of the approved
plan (`--structural` too when it names `data/program.json`). Publish:

1. refuses, before writing anything, unless the overlay is approved
   with a matching hash and is the brief's own overlay; outside a git
   work tree; on a branch with no upstream; when something else is
   already staged; when an `--include` path is not an eligible record;
   or when `README.md` is not the coach's;
2. renders the three pages, refreshes the newest record's regions and,
   with Hevy off, the session sheets;
3. stages exactly `this-week.md`, `README.md`, `progress.md`, the
   overlay, the newest check-in record (or `--record D`), the sheets
   when Hevy is off, and each included path with a change;
4. commits as `coach: publish week of <start> (<overlay id>)` and
   pushes to the branch's upstream, never with `--force`.

A failed push exits 4 and keeps the commit, so the fix is to push by
hand. When nothing differs from the last commit it reports `commit:
null` and pushes nothing. The report lists `records.included`,
`records.unchanged` and `records.local`: eligible records with changes
the plan did not name, which stay out of the commit until you agree. The
coach runs `--dry-run` first and asks about any such path.

A normal clone from GitHub has an upstream. A zip download or a repo you
created with `git init` needs a remote and `git push -u <remote>
<branch>` once, or publishing exits 3.

`/goals` republishes after an approved nutrition change: it validates
the config, renders, and when the brief's overlay is approved publishes
that overlay again, so the phase in the header and the food line in the
brief reach your phone. It never stages `config.toml` or `profile.md`;
those are committed only when you ask.

## Reading the pages on your phone

Your workspace is a private GitHub repository, so open it in the GitHub
app or a browser on your phone: the dashboard is the README GitHub shows
on the repository's front page, and its links open the brief, the
progress page, the latest check-in and the program. Everything on the
phone is what the last `pages publish` pushed; the dashboard's "Updated"
time is that publish's as-of time.
